decisions.summary: Every reader (modal machinery, citations derivation, scripts, tests) reads fragments through the in-memory assembly; pages enumerated from fragment directories
decisions.why: Required for FR-009/US3 AS3: once built pages leave git, nothing but the GM may depend on a build having run. Adds no behavior the GM did not ask for.

decisions.summary: research/site/: home index, one parent page per current page (its opening plus a linked list of its questions), one small page per question and per registry entry, all.html single page
decisions.why: The GM's 'separate parent section ... each of our subsections ... individual pages ... linked on the left' and FR-001/FR-003. A parent page listing its questions is the literal reading of 'parent section' with subsections as their own pages.

decisions.summary: Left navigation drawn from nav.js data by assets/site.js (every parent listed, current expanded and marked, single page linked); no-script fallback is a Contents link
decisions.why: Implements FR-002 and the second message ('the one giant page should be accessible ... in the navigation section to the left'); data-plus-script is an implementation of the requested navigation, priced in R3.

decisions.summary: The old per-page files, citations pages and SOURCES.html are no longer written
decisions.why: The GM asked that what is today separate files become items of one manual; citations move to each small page's foot (fifth message) and into the single page. Not a narrowing: everything they held is in both forms.

decisions.summary: One id index resolves every href per form, unresolved = build failure; small pages allocate notes from 1 with notes and works cited at the foot; single page allocates once with one Citations part; any id collision on the single page refused
decisions.why: FR-004 to FR-007 and the GM's accepted footnote recommendation; the extra collision refusal only enforces that the single page's anchors work.

decisions.summary: make record CHECK=1 builds to a temp dir and exits 1 on any refusal; make citations kept as an alias of make record
decisions.why: FR-011; the alias keeps existing callers working and adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: Modal research links go to research/site/<page>/<id>.html; Entry: lines name fragment paths, read by sources.py and the Entry tooling; 162 lines converted
decisions.why: Second message ('link to the smaller pages') and fifth message (link to the source); FR-008, FR-012.

decisions.summary: .gitignore and git rm --cached of every assembled output incl. glossary.js; push block's record check means 'builds cleanly'
render-sync builds the record in main behind a stamp hashed over tracked research/ files and the build code
decisions.why: Fourth message ('regenerate ... if they would change ... not otherwise'); FR-010. See note on the stamp's input list.

decisions.summary: record-edit-hooks re-aims an Edit on a site page too; sync-with-main refuses an unrelated-history clone, landed before the scrub
decisions.why: The first keeps an existing guard doing its existing job on the new output paths; the second is FR-019.

decisions.summary: Pointer form is the fragment path; sweep script with a review list for inexact matches; resolve check at gate and push with an allowlist for build code that names outputs; make fragment-move moves a fragment and rewrites its pointers; docs updated
decisions.why: Fifth message and the accepted 'pointers name the fragment; a gate check; renames rewrite them'; FR-012 to FR-016. No existing tool renames fragments (fragments.py numbering never renumbers), so the new command is the tooling FR-015 needs.

decisions.summary: Sweep skips specs/*/request.md, READMEs and SOURCE blocks
decisions.why: Implied by the accepted spec's own edge case (the GM's request files left alone as quoted text) and by Principles IV/V: these are the GM's writing, which the session may not edit (source-block and README guards refuse it).

decisions.summary: Sweep skips dev/bypass-log/ and scripts/fixtures/ (recorded command corpora)
decisions.why: Checked separately from the GM-text exclusion. The four matching files are scripts/fixtures/*.json recorded command transcripts used as guard test inputs; a path inside a transcript of a past command is not a link to research, so it is outside the class the GM's rule ('everything linked to research') governs, and rewriting it would falsify a record and change test inputs. The purpose - that a reader following a research link reaches the canonical source - is untouched.

decisions.summary: User-level hook on PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure (Bash), container-detected, fires on every not-found output and every empty existence check incl. dpkg-query and python -m pip show; message tells the session to install rather than work around; self-test with an env override; hooks-test runs it when present
decisions.why: Seventh, ninth and eleventh messages; FR-022 to FR-026. The added forms are inside 'all of the different ways that you would check'.

decisions.summary: GM's other running containers listed through the host-diagnostics client and their ~/.claude mounts read; any without reported to the GM
make done, push, render-sync build on /diagram, git gc --aggressive --prune=now under the sync lock with sizes
decisions.why: Seventh message ('I will have you do the Git GC command yourself'); FR-021.

decisions.summary: After landing: filter-repo in a scratch mirror dropping assembled paths from 0fef1e6f3 on only, tree-for-tree verification, docs/history-rewrite-301.md commit map, live sessions told, GM force-pushes, /diagram reset and repacked, clones replaced with unpushed commits replayed
decisions.why: Sixth and tenth messages and the accepted history recommendation; FR-017 to FR-020. See note on ordering.

decisions.summary: Perf bookends, Inashiro then make maps over the pool, browser look at the site
decisions.why: Verification that the requested thing happened (SC-004 covers the pool's maps); no new behavior.
